name: SEN12-FLOOD: SAR and Multispectral Dataset for Flood Detection
description: SEN12-FLOOD is an earth observation benchmark dataset specifically curated for flood event detection from paired Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 multispectral satellite imagery, created by researchers from the Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers (CNAM), ONERA, and the European Space Agency (ESA). The dataset comprises 336 co-registered observation sequences (totaling 1,947 image-date time slices) capturing major historical flooding events between December 2018 and May 2019 across flood-prone areas in Southern/West Africa, the Middle East (Iran), and Australia. Each tile has a spatial footprint of 512x512 pixels at 10m spatial resolution. By pairing cloud-penetrating synthetic aperture radar (SAR) with optical multispectral bands, SEN12-FLOOD enables all-weather disaster monitoring and multi-modal fusion. Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 pairs represent co-registered observations of the same flood events.

verification.notes: Verified against Source Cooperative (esa/sen12flood), IEEE DataPort (DOI: 10.21227/w6xz-s898), and ISPRS Archives paper. Verified 336 paired observation sequences (1,947 time slices), 512x512 tiles, CC BY 4.0 license, and unified S1/S2 event pairs.

size.notes: Compressed archive payload containing 512x512 GeoTIFF patches for Sentinel-1 (VV, VH) and Sentinel-2 (Level-2A BOA reflectance) with JSON classification labels.

citation.paper_title: Flood Detection in Time Series of Optical and SAR Images

provenance.collection_method: Co-registered time series assembled from Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band synthetic aperture radar and Sentinel-2 multispectral imager observations during recorded flood events.
provenance.curation_notes: Each sequence pairs SAR and optical observations covering the same geographic region; patches are 512x512 pixels at 10m resolution. Labeled for image-level and pixel-level flood presence.
